## A {#glossary-a .unnumbered}

Absorbing state
: A state of a Markov chain that, once entered, is never left. The other states are **transient**. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Adjacency matrix
: A table of connections: entry $(i, j)$ is 1 if item $i$ is linked to item $j$, and 0 otherwise. Its powers count routes. See @sec-matrices and @sec-networks.

Adjugate
: The transpose of the matrix of cofactors. It gives the inverse as $\M{A}^{-1} = \operatorname{adj}\M{A} / \det\M{A}$. See @sec-inverses.

Admittance
: The reciprocal $Y = 1/Z$ of an impedance: the complex version of a conductance, used in nodal analysis of AC circuits. See @sec-circuits.

Affine transformation
: A linear transformation followed by a translation, $\vect{x} \mapsto \M{M}\vect{x} + \vect{t}$. In homogeneous coordinates it is a single matrix. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Algebraic connectivity
: The second smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_2$ of a graph Laplacian. It is zero exactly when the network is in more than one piece, and small when the network has a bottleneck. See @sec-networks.

Algebraic multiplicity
: The number of times an eigenvalue is repeated as a root of the characteristic polynomial. Compare **geometric multiplicity**. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Angle between vectors
: The angle $\theta$ with $\vect{x} \cdot \vect{y} = \lVert\vect{x}\rVert\,\lVert\vect{y}\rVert\cos\theta$. It makes sense in any number of dimensions because of the **Cauchy–Schwarz inequality**. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Approximate minimum degree
: A fast way of reordering the unknowns of a sparse system before factorising it, chosen to keep fill-in small. Compare **nested dissection**. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Augmented matrix
: The matrix $[\M{A} \mid \vect{b}]$ formed by adding the right-hand side of a linear system as an extra column. See @sec-linear-systems and @sec-gaussian-elimination.

## B {#glossary-b .unnumbered}

Back substitution
: Solving an upper triangular system from the last equation upwards. See @sec-gaussian-elimination.

Backward error analysis
: Judging a method by asking whether its computed answer is the exact answer to a slightly different problem, with a change in the data about as small as the rounding errors in storing it. If so, the method is **backward stable**. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Backward stable
: Describes a method whose computed answer is the exact answer to a problem within rounding error of the one posed. Its remaining error is then due only to the problem's conditioning. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Banded matrix
: A matrix whose non-zero entries all lie within a fixed distance of the main diagonal. Elimination without row swaps keeps the band. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Basin of attraction
: The set of starting points from which an iterative method, such as Newton's method, reaches a particular solution. See @sec-newton-systems.

Basis
: A set of linearly independent vectors that spans a subspace. Every vector in the subspace is a combination of them in exactly one way. See @sec-basis-change.

BiCGSTAB
: A Krylov method for large sparse systems whose matrix is not symmetric. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Bidiagonal matrix
: A matrix whose only non-zero entries are on the main diagonal and just above it. Computing the SVD starts by reducing a matrix to this form with Householder reflections. See @sec-qr-least-squares.

Block diagonal matrix
: A matrix made of square blocks down the main diagonal, with zeros everywhere else. The Laplacian of a network in separate pieces has this form when the nodes of each piece are numbered together. See @sec-networks.

Block tridiagonal matrix
: A matrix whose blocks follow a tridiagonal pattern: non-zero blocks only on the diagonal and just above and below it. The five-point stencil gives this form. See @sec-finite-differences.

Broyden's method
: A quasi-Newton method for systems of equations, which avoids computing the Jacobian at every step. See @sec-newton-systems.

## C {#glossary-c .unnumbered}

Cancellation
: The loss of accuracy when two nearly equal numbers are subtracted, leaving only their uncertain digits. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
: $\lvert\vect{x} \cdot \vect{y}\rvert \le \lVert\vect{x}\rVert\,\lVert\vect{y}\rVert$, in any number of dimensions. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Central difference
: The approximation $u''(x) \approx \bigl(u(x - h) - 2u(x) + u(x + h)\bigr)/h^2$ to a second derivative, using a point and its two neighbours. See @sec-finite-differences.

Centre
: An equilibrium of $\dot{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\vect{x}$ surrounded by closed orbits, which happens when the eigenvalues are purely imaginary. See @sec-linear-odes.

Chain rule
: For functions of several variables, the derivative of a composition is the product of the Jacobians: the chain rule becomes matrix multiplication. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Characteristic equation
: The equation $\det(\M{A} - \lambda\M{I}) = 0$, whose solutions are the eigenvalues of $\M{A}$. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Characteristic polynomial
: The polynomial $\det(\M{A} - \lambda\M{I})$, whose roots are the eigenvalues of $\M{A}$. Setting it to zero gives the **characteristic equation**. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Cholesky factorisation
: The factorisation $\M{A} = \M{L}\M{L}\T$ of a symmetric positive definite matrix, with $\M{L}$ lower triangular with positive diagonal entries. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Coefficient of determination
: $R^2$: the fraction of the variation in the data that a regression model explains. See @sec-data-science.

Cofactor
: The determinant left after crossing out row $i$ and column $j$ of a square matrix (the **minor**), multiplied by $(-1)^{i+j}$. See @sec-determinants and @sec-inverses.

Cofactor expansion
: Working out a determinant along a row or column: multiply each entry by its cofactor and add. See @sec-determinants.

Collinearity
: Near-dependence between the explanatory variables in a regression, which makes the design matrix ill-conditioned and the coefficients unreliable. See @sec-data-science.

Column space
: The span of the columns of a matrix: every vector $\M{A}\vect{x}$. $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$ has a solution exactly when $\vect{b}$ is in it. See @sec-fundamental-subspaces.

Column vector
: A matrix with one column. In this book, vectors are columns unless they are transposed. See @sec-matrices.

Column-stochastic matrix
: A matrix with no negative entries whose columns each add up to 1, such as the transition matrix of a Markov chain. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Complete pivoting
: Choosing each pivot as the largest entry, in size, in the whole of the remaining submatrix, and swapping both rows and columns to bring it into place. Compare **partial pivoting**. See @sec-pivoting.

Composition
: Doing one transformation after another. "Apply $\M{B}$, then $\M{A}$" has matrix $\M{A}\M{B}$. See @sec-composition.

Compressed sparse row (CSR)
: The most common way of storing a sparse matrix, using three lists: the non-zero values, their column numbers, and where each row starts. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Compression
: The state of a truss member that is being pushed along its length. Compare **tension**. See @sec-trusses.

Condition number
: For a square matrix, the ratio $\sigma_1/\sigma_n$ of its largest to smallest singular value. It measures how much errors can be magnified when solving $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$. See @sec-svd-pca and @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Conductance matrix
: The symmetric matrix $\M{G}$ of nodal analysis, with $\M{G}\vect{v} = \vect{i}$ relating node voltages to injected currents; $\M{G} = \M{A}\T\M{C}\M{A}$. See @sec-circuits.

Conjugate gradient method
: An iterative method for symmetric positive definite systems that minimises $\tfrac{1}{2}\vect{x}\T\M{A}\vect{x} - \vect{b}\T\vect{x}$ along mutually conjugate directions. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Conjugate pairs
: Complex eigenvalues of a real matrix always come in pairs $\alpha \pm i\beta$, because the characteristic polynomial has real coefficients. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Connected component
: A piece of a network in which every node can reach every other by following edges. The number of components is the number of zero eigenvalues of the graph Laplacian. See @sec-networks.

Consistent system
: A system of equations with at least one solution. One with no solution is **inconsistent**. See @sec-linear-systems.

Continuation
: Solving a sequence of problems that change gradually from an easy one to the one you want, starting each from the last answer, to give Newton's method good starting guesses. See @sec-newton-systems.

Coordinates
: The coefficients that write a vector as a combination of the vectors of a basis. See @sec-basis-change.

Covariance matrix
: For data with $p$ variables, the $p \times p$ symmetric matrix whose entry $(i, j)$ is the covariance of variables $i$ and $j$, with the variances on the diagonal. See @sec-symmetric-matrices and @sec-svd-pca.

Cubic convergence
: Convergence in which the number of correct digits roughly triples at each step, as in Rayleigh quotient iteration for symmetric matrices. Compare **quadratic convergence**. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

## D {#glossary-d .unnumbered}

Damping
: (1) In PageRank, following a link with probability $d$ and jumping to a random page otherwise, which makes the chain regular. See @sec-markov-pagerank. (2) In vibrations, a friction-like force $\M{C}\dot{\vect{x}}$ that removes energy and keeps resonant peaks finite. See @sec-vibrations.

Defective matrix
: A square matrix without enough independent eigenvectors to form a basis, such as a shear. It can't be diagonalised. See @sec-eigenvalues and @sec-diagonalisation.

Deflation
: Once an eigenvalue has converged, removing the last row and column and carrying on with a smaller matrix. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Degree
: The number of edges at a node of a network: the sum of its row of the adjacency matrix. See @sec-networks.

Denavit–Hartenberg convention
: The standard way of setting out a robot arm in three dimensions, with one $4 \times 4$ matrix per joint. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Dependence relation
: A combination of vectors that adds up to $\zerovec$ without all the coefficients being zero. Vectors are **linearly dependent** exactly when one exists. See @sec-span-independence.

Design matrix
: The matrix $\M{X}$ of a linear model $\vect{y} \approx \M{X}\vect{\beta}$: a column of 1s for the intercept and one column per explanatory variable. See @sec-data-science.

Determinant
: The factor by which a square matrix scales areas (in 2D) or volumes (in 3D), with a negative sign when it reverses orientation. See @sec-determinants.

Diagonal matrix
: A square matrix whose entries off the main diagonal are all zero. It stretches space along the axes. See @sec-transformations.

Diagonalisation
: Writing $\M{A} = \M{P}\M{D}\M{P}^{-1}$, with the eigenvectors of $\M{A}$ as the columns of $\M{P}$ and its eigenvalues on the diagonal of $\M{D}$. See @sec-diagonalisation.

Diagonally dominant
: Describes a matrix whose diagonal entry in each row is larger in size than the sum of the sizes of the other entries in that row (strictly diagonally dominant), or at least as large. See @sec-iterative-methods and @sec-pivoting.

Dimension
: The number of vectors in any basis of a subspace: 1 for a line, 2 for a plane, $n$ for $\R^n$. See @sec-basis-change.

Direct intensity
: The amount of a pollutant, such as carbon dioxide, that a sector emits for each £1 of its own output. Compare **footprint**. See @sec-input-output.

Direct method
: A method that gives the answer, up to rounding, after a fixed number of steps, such as Gaussian elimination. Compare **iterative method**. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Distance
: The distance between $\vect{x}$ and $\vect{y}$ is $\lVert\vect{x} - \vect{y}\rVert$. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Dominant eigenvalue
: The eigenvalue of largest absolute value, when it is strictly larger than all the others. It decides the long-run behaviour of $\M{A}^k\vect{x}$. See @sec-diagonalisation.

Dot product
: For two lists of numbers of the same length, the sum of the products of matching entries: $(1, 2, 3) \cdot (4, 5, 6) = 4 + 10 + 18 = 32$. See the [Refresher](../front/refresher.qmd) and @sec-multiplication.

Double precision
: The standard floating-point format, which keeps 53 binary digits (about 16 decimal digits) and handles numbers up to about $10^{308}$. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Driving frequency
: The frequency $\Omega$ of a force that pushes a structure back and forth, $\vect{f}\cos(\Omega t)$. See @sec-vibrations.

## E {#glossary-e .unnumbered}

Eckart–Young theorem
: Keeping the $k$ largest singular values of the SVD gives the closest matrix of rank $k$, measuring closeness by the square root of the sum of the squared differences of the entries. See @sec-svd-pca.

Edge
: A connection between two nodes of a network. See @sec-networks.

Eigenspace
: All the eigenvectors for one eigenvalue $\lambda$, together with $\zerovec$: the null space of $\M{A} - \lambda\M{I}$. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Eigenvalue
: A number $\lambda$ for which $\M{A}\vect{v} = \lambda\vect{v}$ has a non-zero solution $\vect{v}$, the **eigenvector**: the factor by which $\M{A}$ stretches that direction. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Eigenvector
: A non-zero vector that a matrix only stretches (or flips), so that it stays on the same line through the origin: $\M{A}\vect{v} = \lambda\vect{v}$. The number $\lambda$ is the matching **eigenvalue**. See @sec-invariant-lines and @sec-eigenvalues.

Eigenvector centrality
: A measure of how important each node of a network is: the entries of the eigenvector of the adjacency matrix for its largest eigenvalue. A node scores highly if its neighbours do. See @sec-networks.

Elasticity
: In population models, the proportional change in the growth rate $\lambda$ for a proportional change in one matrix entry. See @sec-population-models.

Enlargement
: The transformation $k\M{I}$, which scales every vector by $k$ about the origin. See @sec-transformations.

Entry
: One of the numbers in a matrix. The entry in row $i$ and column $j$ of $\M{A}$ is written $a_{ij}$. See @sec-matrices.

Equal matrices
: Two matrices are equal when they have the same size and every pair of corresponding entries is equal. See @sec-matrices.

Equilibration
: Dividing each row of a system by its largest entry before elimination, so that all rows have similar sizes. See @sec-pivoting.

Equilibrium
: A state that does not change. For $\dot{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\vect{x}$, the origin is an equilibrium, and it is **stable** if every solution tends to it. See @sec-linear-odes.

Equilibrium matrix
: The matrix whose columns give the forces that each member force and reaction exerts on the joints of a truss. See @sec-trusses.

## F {#glossary-f .unnumbered}

Fecundity
: In a population model, the average number of female offspring, surviving to the next count, produced by each female in a class: the first row of a Leslie matrix. See @sec-population-models.

Fiedler vector
: The eigenvector of a graph Laplacian for its second smallest eigenvalue. The signs of its entries split the network into two well-separated groups. See @sec-networks.

Fill-in
: New non-zero entries created in the factors of a sparse matrix during elimination. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Final demand
: What households, the government and other countries buy from a sector, as opposed to what other sectors buy. See @sec-input-output.

Finite difference
: An approximation to a derivative from values at neighbouring grid points, such as $u'' \approx (u_{i-1} - 2u_i + u_{i+1})/h^2$. See @sec-finite-differences.

Finite difference method
: Replacing the derivatives in a differential equation by differences between values on a grid, which turns it into a linear system. See @sec-finite-differences.

Five-point stencil
: The finite difference version of Laplace's equation on a square grid, $4u_{i,j} - u_{i-1,j} - u_{i+1,j} - u_{i,j-1} - u_{i,j+1} = 0$: each value is the average of its four neighbours. See @sec-finite-differences.

Floating-point number
: A number stored as $\pm m \times 2^e$ with a fixed number of binary digits in $m$; double precision keeps about 16 significant decimal digits. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Flops
: Floating-point operations. A method's running time is roughly proportional to the number of flops it needs. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Footprint
: The total amount of a pollutant emitted, anywhere in the economy, to deliver £1 of a sector's product to a final buyer. Compare **direct intensity**. See @sec-input-output.

Forward kinematics
: Finding the position and orientation of a robot's hand from its joint angles, as a product of transformation matrices. The reverse problem is **inverse kinematics**. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Forward substitution
: Solving a lower triangular system from the first equation downwards. See @sec-lu-decomposition.

Free variable
: An unknown whose column has no pivot in the reduced row echelon form. It can take any value, and the **pivot variables** are then found from it. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Fundamental matrix
: For an absorbing Markov chain, $\M{N} = (\M{I} - \M{Q})^{-1}$, where $\M{Q}$ holds the probabilities of moving between transient states. Its entries are expected numbers of visits, its column sums the expected times until absorption. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

## G {#glossary-g .unnumbered}

Gauss–Jordan elimination
: Elimination continued until the matrix reaches reduced row echelon form, so that the solution can be read straight off. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Gauss–Seidel method
: An iterative method that solves each equation for its own unknown, using the newest values of the others as soon as they are available. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Generalised eigenvalue problem
: The problem $\M{K}\vect{v} = \lambda\M{M}\vect{v}$, with a matrix $\M{M}$ in place of $\M{I}$. See @sec-vibrations.

Geometric multiplicity
: The dimension of the eigenspace of an eigenvalue: the number of independent eigenvectors it has. It is never more than the **algebraic multiplicity**. See @sec-eigenvalues.

GMRES
: A Krylov method for large sparse systems whose matrix is not symmetric. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Google matrix
: The matrix $\M{G} = d\M{M} + \frac{1 - d}{n}\vect{1}\vect{1}\T$ used by PageRank, which mixes following links with jumping to a random page. Its entries are all positive, so it has a unique steady state. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Gradient
: The column vector $\nabla f$ of the partial derivatives of a scalar function $f(\vect{x})$. It points in the direction of steepest increase, perpendicular to the contours. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Gradient descent
: Minimising a function by repeatedly stepping in the direction of $-\nabla f$. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Gram–Schmidt process
: A method for turning independent vectors into orthonormal vectors with the same span. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Graph Laplacian
: The matrix $\M{L} = \M{D} - \M{A}$ of a network, with the degrees of the nodes on its diagonal and $-1$ for each edge. It is symmetric positive semidefinite, with one zero eigenvalue for each piece of the network. See @sec-networks.

Ground
: The reference node of a circuit, whose voltage is taken to be 0. See @sec-circuits.

Growth factor
: The largest entry produced during elimination divided by the largest entry of the original matrix. Large growth magnifies rounding errors. See @sec-pivoting.

Growth rate
: In a population model, the dominant eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ of the matrix: in the long run the population grows by a factor $\lambda_1$ each step. See @sec-population-models.

## H {#glossary-h .unnumbered}

Hamiltonian
: The Hermitian matrix $\M{H}$ representing the energy of a quantum system. It determines how the state changes in time, through the Schrödinger equation. See @sec-physics.

Hermitian matrix
: A complex square matrix equal to its conjugate transpose: the complex version of a symmetric matrix. Its eigenvalues are real. See @sec-physics.

Hessenberg form
: A matrix that is zero below the first subdiagonal (tridiagonal, if the matrix is symmetric). The QR algorithm reduces a matrix to this form first, so that each step is cheaper. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Hessian
: The symmetric matrix of second partial derivatives $\partial^2 f/\partial x_i\partial x_j$ of a scalar function. Its eigenvalues classify stationary points. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Hilbert matrix
: The $n \times n$ matrix with entries $h_{ij} = 1/(i + j - 1)$, a standard example of an ill-conditioned matrix. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Hill cipher
: A cipher that encrypts blocks of letters by multiplying them by a key matrix modulo 26. See @sec-cryptography.

Homogeneous coordinates
: Representing the point $(x, y)$ as $(x, y, 1)$ (or $(x, y, z)$ as $(x, y, z, 1)$), so that translations and perspective become matrix multiplications. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Homogeneous system
: A system $\M{A}\vect{x} = \zerovec$, with every right-hand side zero. It always has the solution $\vect{x} = \zerovec$. See @sec-linear-systems.

Householder QR
: Computing a QR factorisation with Householder reflections, the way elimination uses row operations. It is backward stable. See @sec-qr-least-squares.

Householder reflection
: The orthogonal matrix $\M{I} - 2\vect{v}\vect{v}\T/(\vect{v}\T\vect{v})$, a reflection, chosen to zero all but the first entry of a vector. See @sec-qr-least-squares.

## I {#glossary-i .unnumbered}

Identity matrix
: The square matrix $\M{I}$ with 1 on the main diagonal and 0 elsewhere. Multiplying by it changes nothing. See @sec-multiplication.

Ill-conditioned
: Describes a problem whose answer changes a lot when its data change a little, such as a system with a large condition number. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Impedance
: The complex number that plays the part of resistance for a capacitor or inductor at angular frequency $\omega$: $Z_C = 1/(j\omega C)$ and $Z_L = j\omega L$. See @sec-circuits.

Incidence matrix
: For a network, the matrix with one row per edge, holding $+1$ and $-1$ in the columns of the two nodes it joins. See @sec-circuits.

Inconsistent system
: A system of equations with no solution. See **consistent system** and @sec-linear-systems.

Inertia tensor
: The symmetric matrix $\M{I}$ with $\vect{L} = \M{I}\vect{\omega}$, relating a rigid body's angular velocity to its angular momentum. Its eigenvectors are the **principal axes**. See @sec-physics.

Input–output table
: A table recording how much each industry buys from every other, the starting point of Leontief's model of an economy. See @sec-input-output.

Invariant line
: A line that a transformation maps onto itself, though the points on it may move along it. See @sec-invariant-lines.

Invariant point
: A point that a transformation leaves where it is: $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{x}$. A whole line of them is a **line of invariant points**. See @sec-invariant-lines.

Inverse
: The matrix $\M{A}^{-1}$ that undoes $\M{A}$, so that $\M{A}^{-1}\M{A} = \M{I}$. See @sec-inverses.

Inverse iteration
: The power method applied to $(\M{A} - \mu\M{I})^{-1}$, which finds the eigenvalue of $\M{A}$ closest to the shift $\mu$. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Inverse kinematics
: Finding the joint angles that put a robot's hand at a chosen point: the reverse of **forward kinematics**. It is usually solved by Newton's method. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Inverse modulo n
: A number $a^{-1}$ with $aa^{-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, which exists exactly when $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. See @sec-cryptography.

Invertible matrix
: A square matrix that has an inverse; the same as a non-singular matrix. See @sec-inverses.

Iteration matrix
: The matrix $\M{T}$ in an iteration $\vect{x}_{k+1} = \M{T}\vect{x}_k + \vect{c}$; the error is multiplied by $\M{T}$ at each step. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Iterative method
: A method that starts from a guess and improves it step by step until it is accurate enough, such as Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel or conjugate gradients. Compare **direct method**. See @sec-iterative-methods.

## J {#glossary-j .unnumbered}

Jacobi method
: An iterative method that solves each equation for its own unknown, using the previous values of all the others. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Jacobian
: The $m \times n$ matrix of partial derivatives $\partial f_i/\partial x_j$ of a function from $\R^n$ to $\R^m$: the matrix of its best linear approximation at a point. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Joint
: A point of a truss where members meet. See @sec-trusses.

## K {#glossary-k .unnumbered}

Key matrix
: The matrix $\M{K}$ that a Hill cipher multiplies each block of letters by. See @sec-cryptography.

Kirchhoff's current law
: At every node of a circuit, the total current flowing out equals the total current flowing in. See @sec-circuits.

Kirchhoff's voltage law
: Around any closed loop of a circuit, the voltage changes add up to zero. See @sec-circuits.

Known-plaintext attack
: Recovering a cipher's key from a piece of message whose plain and encrypted versions are both known. See @sec-cryptography.

Kronecker product
: The block matrix $\M{A} \otimes \M{B}$ whose $(i, j)$ block is $a_{ij}\M{B}$; it builds the matrices of grid problems in two and three dimensions. See @sec-finite-differences.

Krylov method
: An iterative method that builds its answer from the vectors $\vect{b}, \M{A}\vect{b}, \M{A}^2\vect{b}, \dots$, such as conjugate gradients, GMRES and BiCGSTAB for linear systems, and Lanczos and Arnoldi for eigenvalues. See @sec-iterative-methods and @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

## L {#glossary-l .unnumbered}

Laplace's equation
: The equation $\partial^2 u/\partial x^2 + \partial^2 u/\partial y^2 = 0$, satisfied by the steady temperature in a plate with no heat sources. See @sec-finite-differences.

Leading principal minor
: The determinant of a top-left $k \times k$ block of a matrix. A symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when all of them are positive. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Learning rate
: Another name for the **step size** in gradient descent. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Least squares
: Choosing $\vect{x}$ to make the sum of the squares of the errors in $\M{A}\vect{x} \approx \vect{b}$ as small as possible, by solving the normal equations. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Least-squares solution
: The vector $\hat{\vect{x}}$ that makes $\lVert\M{A}\vect{x} - \vect{b}\rVert^2$ as small as possible. See **least squares** and @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Lefkovitch matrix
: A population matrix based on stages (such as eggs, juveniles and adults) rather than ages, with fecundities in the first row, the chances of staying in each stage on the diagonal, and the chances of growing into the next stage below it. See @sec-population-models.

Left eigenvector
: A non-zero vector $\vect{v}$ with $\vect{v}\T\M{A} = \lambda\vect{v}\T$: an eigenvector of $\M{A}\T$. See @sec-population-models.

Left null space
: The null space of $\M{A}\T$: the combinations of the rows of $\M{A}$ that add up to zero. See @sec-fundamental-subspaces.

Left singular vectors
: The columns $\vect{u}_i$ of $\M{U}$ in the SVD $\M{A} = \M{U}\M{\Sigma}\M{V}\T$: the perpendicular output directions. See @sec-svd-pca.

Leontief inverse
: The matrix $(\M{I} - \M{A})^{-1}$ of an input–output model, giving the total output, direct and indirect, needed from each industry for each £1 of final demand. See @sec-input-output.

Leslie matrix
: A population projection matrix with fecundities in its first row and survival rates just below the diagonal. See @sec-diagonalisation and @sec-population-models.

Line of invariant points
: A line every point of which a transformation leaves where it is, such as the mirror of a reflection or the axis of a rotation in three dimensions. A **plane of invariant points** is the same in a plane. See @sec-invariant-lines.

Line search
: In Newton's method, trying half the step, then a quarter, and so on, whenever the full step makes the equations further from being satisfied. See @sec-newton-systems.

Linear combination
: A sum of scaled vectors, such as $s\vect{a} + t\vect{b}$. See @sec-arithmetic.

Linear equation
: An equation in which the unknowns are only multiplied by numbers and added, such as $3x + 2y - z = 1$. See @sec-matrices and @sec-linear-systems.

Linear independence
: Vectors are linearly independent if no combination of them gives $\zerovec$ except the one with all coefficients zero. Otherwise they are **linearly dependent**, and one of them is a combination of the others. See @sec-span-independence.

Linear model
: A prediction $y \approx \beta_0 + \beta_1x_1 + \dots + \beta_px_p$ of one quantity from others, fitted by least squares. See @sec-data-science.

Linear transformation
: A transformation with $\M{A}(s\vect{x} + t\vect{y}) = s\M{A}\vect{x} + t\M{A}\vect{y}$. Every matrix gives one, and in the plane or space every one is given by a matrix. See @sec-transformations.

Linearly dependent
: See **linear independence** and **dependence relation**.

Loadings
: The entries of a principal component, which say how much each original variable contributes to it. See @sec-data-science.

Lower triangular matrix
: See **triangular matrix**.

Low-pass filter
: A circuit that lets slowly varying signals through but weakens fast ones. See @sec-circuits.

Low-rank approximation
: A matrix of rank $k$ close to a given matrix. Keeping the first $k$ terms of the SVD gives the closest one (the Eckart–Young theorem). See @sec-svd-pca.

LU decomposition
: Writing a square matrix as $\M{A} = \M{L}\M{U}$, with $\M{L}$ lower triangular (holding the multipliers of elimination) and $\M{U}$ upper triangular. With row swaps, $\M{P}\M{A} = \M{L}\M{U}$. See @sec-lu-decomposition.

## M {#glossary-m .unnumbered}

Machine epsilon
: The gap between 1 and the next larger floating-point number, about $2.2 \times 10^{-16}$ in double precision. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Main diagonal
: The entries $a_{11}, a_{22}, \dots$ of a square matrix, running from top left to bottom right. See @sec-matrices.

Markov chain
: A process that moves between states at random, with probabilities that depend only on the current state, described by $\vect{x}_{k+1} = \M{M}\vect{x}_k$ with a matrix whose columns add to 1. See @sec-diagonalisation and @sec-markov-pagerank.

Mass matrix
: The matrix $\M{M}$ in $\M{M}\ddot{\vect{x}} + \M{K}\vect{x} = \zerovec$; for point masses it is $\operatorname{diag}(m_1, \dots, m_n)$. See @sec-vibrations.

Matrix
: A rectangular array of numbers. An $m \times n$ matrix has $m$ rows and $n$ columns. See @sec-matrices.

Matrix exponential
: The matrix $e^{\M{A}t} = \M{I} + \M{A}t + (\M{A}t)^2/2! + \cdots$, which solves $\dot{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\vect{x}$ as $\vect{x}(t) = e^{\M{A}t}\vect{x}_0$. See @sec-linear-odes.

Mechanism
: A structure that can move without any member changing length; its equilibrium matrix doesn't have full row rank, and its stiffness matrix is singular. See @sec-trusses.

Member
: One of the straight bars of a truss, joined at its ends to joints and carrying only tension or compression. See @sec-trusses.

Minor
: The determinant of the matrix left when the row and column of an entry are crossed out. With a sign attached, it is the **cofactor**. See @sec-determinants.

Mode
: A pattern that evolves on its own in a linear system: an eigenvector, multiplied by $\lambda^k$ in a discrete process or by $e^{\lambda t}$ in a continuous one. See @sec-diagonalisation and @sec-linear-odes.

Mode shape
: The pattern in which a structure moves when it vibrates at one of its natural frequencies: an eigenvector of $\M{K}\vect{v} = \omega^2\M{M}\vect{v}$. See @sec-vibrations.

Model matrix
: The matrix that places an object in a 3D scene, setting its position, orientation and size. Compare **view matrix**. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Modified Gram–Schmidt
: A rearrangement of the Gram–Schmidt process that subtracts each component from all the remaining columns as soon as it is found. In floating point it keeps the vectors much closer to perpendicular than the classical version. See @sec-qr-least-squares.

Modified nodal analysis
: Nodal analysis extended with the currents through voltage sources as extra unknowns. See @sec-circuits.

Modular arithmetic
: Arithmetic in which only the remainder on division by a fixed number is kept, as modulo 26 in the Hill cipher. See **inverse modulo n** and @sec-cryptography.

Moments of inertia
: The diagonal entries of the inertia tensor, such as $I_{xx} = \sum m(y^2 + z^2)$. The off-diagonal entries are the **products of inertia**, and the eigenvalues are the **principal moments of inertia**. See @sec-physics.

Multiple regression
: Predicting one quantity from several others with a linear model, fitted by least squares. See @sec-data-science.

Multiplier
: In Gaussian elimination, the number $m_{ik} = a_{ik}/a_{kk}$ such that subtracting $m_{ik}$ times the pivot row clears the entry below the pivot. See @sec-gaussian-elimination.

## N {#glossary-n .unnumbered}

Natural frequency
: A frequency at which a structure vibrates freely when disturbed. The natural frequencies $\omega$ of a system of masses and springs solve $\det(\M{K} - \omega^2\M{M}) = 0$. See @sec-vibrations.

Nested dissection
: A way of reordering the unknowns of a sparse system before factorising it, chosen to keep fill-in small. Compare **approximate minimum degree**. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Network
: A set of nodes joined by edges, such as friendships, web pages or roads between towns. See @sec-networks.

Newton's method
: Solving $\vect{f}(\vect{x}) = \zerovec$ by repeatedly solving the linear system $\M{J}(\vect{x}_k)\,\Delta\vect{x} = -\vect{f}(\vect{x}_k)$ and setting $\vect{x}_{k+1} = \vect{x}_k + \Delta\vect{x}$. See @sec-newton-systems.

Node
: (1) A point of a network or circuit where edges or components join. See @sec-networks and @sec-circuits. (2) An equilibrium of $\dot{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\vect{x}$ whose eigenvalues are real with the same sign: stable if both are negative. See @sec-linear-odes.

Norm
: A measure of the size of a vector, such as the length $\lVert\vect{x}\rVert_2$ or the largest entry $\lVert\vect{x}\rVert_\infty$; for a matrix, the most it stretches any vector. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares and @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Normal equations
: $\M{A}\T\M{A}\hat{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\T\vect{b}$, whose solution is the least-squares solution of $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Normal stress
: A diagonal entry of a stress matrix: a pull ($+$) or push ($-$) straight across a surface. Compare **shear stress**. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Null space
: All the solutions of $\M{A}\vect{x} = \zerovec$. Its dimension is the **nullity**. See @sec-fundamental-subspaces.

## O {#glossary-o .unnumbered}

Orientation
: Whether a transformation keeps the plane or space the same way round, or turns it into its mirror image. It is recorded by the sign of the determinant. See @sec-determinants.

Orthogonal matrix
: A square matrix $\M{Q}$ with $\M{Q}\T\M{Q} = \M{I}$. It preserves lengths and angles: a rotation or a reflection. See @sec-inverses.

Orthogonal vectors
: Vectors at right angles: their dot product is zero. **Orthonormal** vectors are orthogonal and of length 1. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Orthonormal vectors
: Vectors that each have length 1 and are perpendicular in pairs. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Output multiplier
: The total output across a whole economy generated by £1 of final demand for one sector: a column sum of the Leontief inverse. See @sec-input-output.

Overdetermined system
: A system with more equations than unknowns. It usually has no solution, and is solved by least squares instead. Compare **underdetermined system**. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

## P {#glossary-p .unnumbered}

PageRank
: The steady state of a random surfer on the web, following links with probability $d$ and jumping to a random page otherwise. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Parallelepiped
: The slanted box with three vectors as its edges. The size of the determinant of the matrix with those columns is its volume. See @sec-determinants.

Partial pivoting
: Swapping rows during elimination so that each pivot is the largest entry, in size, in its column on or below the diagonal. See @sec-lu-decomposition and @sec-pivoting.

Particular solution
: Any one solution of $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$. Every solution is a particular solution plus a solution of $\M{A}\vect{x} = \zerovec$. See @sec-linear-systems.

Pauli matrices
: The $2 \times 2$ Hermitian matrices that represent measurements of spin along the three axes in quantum mechanics. See @sec-physics.

Permutation matrix
: The identity matrix with its rows in a different order. Multiplying by it reorders the rows of a matrix. See @sec-lu-decomposition.

Perpendicular axis theorem
: For a flat body, the moment of inertia about the axis perpendicular to it is the sum of the moments about two perpendicular axes in its plane. See @sec-physics.

Perspective projection
: The projection that makes distant objects look smaller: a point at depth $-z$ in front of a camera with focal length $d$ appears at $(dx/(-z), \; dy/(-z))$. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Phase portrait
: A picture of the paths followed by the solutions of a system of two differential equations in the plane. See @sec-linear-odes.

Phasor
: A complex number representing a sinusoidal voltage or current: its size is the amplitude and its angle is the phase. See @sec-circuits.

Pin
: A truss support that can push in any direction, so it provides two unknown reaction components. Compare **roller**. See @sec-trusses.

Pivot
: The entry used to clear the others in its column during elimination: in echelon form, the first non-zero entry of each row. It must not be zero, and in practice should not be small. See @sec-gaussian-elimination and @sec-pivoting.

Pivot columns
: The columns of a matrix that contain pivots after elimination. The original vectors in these columns form a basis for the column space. See @sec-basis-change and @sec-fundamental-subspaces.

Pivot variables
: The unknowns whose columns contain a pivot, also called basic variables. The others are **free variables**. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Positive definite matrix
: A symmetric matrix with $\vect{x}\T\M{A}\vect{x} > 0$ for every $\vect{x} \neq \zerovec$; equivalently, with all eigenvalues positive. **Positive semidefinite** allows $\ge 0$. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Positive semidefinite matrix
: A symmetric matrix with $\vect{x}\T\M{A}\vect{x} \ge 0$ for every $\vect{x}$: its eigenvalues are all at least 0. $\M{A}\T\M{A}$ is always positive semidefinite. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Power method
: Finding the dominant eigenvector by repeatedly multiplying a vector by $\M{A}$ and rescaling it. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Preconditioner
: An approximation $\M{M}$ to $\M{A}$, easy to solve with, used to transform a system so that iterative methods converge faster. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Principal axes
: The eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix, such as those of a quadratic form or an inertia tensor: the perpendicular directions along which it acts as a pure stretch. See @sec-symmetric-matrices and @sec-physics.

Principal component analysis
: Describing data by its coordinates along the directions of greatest variance, the **principal components**: the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, or the right singular vectors of the centred data. See @sec-svd-pca.

Principal components
: The directions of greatest spread in a set of data: the eigenvectors of its covariance matrix, or the right singular vectors of the centred data matrix. See @sec-svd-pca.

Principal directions
: The eigenvectors of a stress matrix, along which there is no shear stress. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Principal stresses
: The eigenvalues of a stress matrix: the normal stresses along the perpendicular directions in which there is no shear. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Productive economy
: An economy in which $\M{I} - \M{A}$ has an inverse with no negative entries, so that it can meet any final demand. See @sec-input-output.

Projection
: The closest point to a vector in a line or subspace, found by dropping a perpendicular. See @sec-transformations and @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Projection matrix
: The matrix $\M{P} = \M{A}(\M{A}\T\M{A})^{-1}\M{A}\T$ that projects any vector onto the column space of $\M{A}$. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares.

Pseudoinverse
: The matrix $\M{A}^+ = \M{V}\M{\Sigma}^+\M{U}\T$, built from the SVD by inverting the non-zero singular values. $\M{A}^+\vect{b}$ is the shortest least-squares solution of $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$. See @sec-svd-pca.

## Q {#glossary-q .unnumbered}

QR algorithm
: The standard method for computing all eigenvalues: factorise $\M{A}_k = \M{Q}_k\M{R}_k$, set $\M{A}_{k+1} = \M{R}_k\M{Q}_k$, and repeat. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

QR factorisation
: Writing $\M{A} = \M{Q}\M{R}$, with $\M{Q}$ having orthonormal columns and $\M{R}$ upper triangular. See @sec-orthogonality-least-squares and @sec-qr-least-squares.

Quadratic convergence
: Convergence in which each error is roughly proportional to the square of the previous one, so the number of correct digits roughly doubles at each step. See @sec-newton-systems.

Quadratic form
: A function $\vect{x}\T\M{A}\vect{x}$ with $\M{A}$ symmetric, such as $ax^2 + 2bxy + cy^2$. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

## R {#glossary-r .unnumbered}

$\R^n$
: The set of all vectors with $n$ real-number entries: the plane is $\R^2$ and ordinary space is $\R^3$. See @sec-span-independence.

Rabi oscillation
: The flipping back and forth of a quantum spin between two states, the basis of MRI and of single-qubit operations in quantum computers. See @sec-physics.

Rank
: The number of pivots in the echelon form of a matrix: the number of independent rows. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Rank–nullity theorem
: For a matrix with $n$ columns, rank plus nullity equals $n$. See @sec-fundamental-subspaces.

Rayleigh quotient
: The estimate $\vect{q}\T\M{A}\vect{q}$ of an eigenvalue, for an approximate eigenvector $\vect{q}$ of length 1. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Rayleigh quotient iteration
: Shifted inverse iteration that uses the current Rayleigh quotient as the shift at every step. For symmetric matrices it converges cubically. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Reactions
: The forces that a structure's supports provide. See @sec-trusses.

Reduced row echelon form
: A row echelon form in which every pivot is 1 and is the only non-zero entry in its column. Each matrix has exactly one. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Redundant member
: A member of a statically indeterminate truss beyond those needed for equilibrium. A truss with $m$ members, $r$ reaction components and $j$ joints has $m + r - 2j$ of them. See @sec-trusses.

Regular Markov chain
: A Markov chain some power of whose transition matrix has all its entries positive. It has a unique steady state, which every starting distribution approaches. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Reproductive value
: An entry of the left eigenvector of a population matrix: how much an individual in that stage will contribute to the future population. See @sec-population-models.

Residual
: The vector $\vect{b} - \M{A}\hat{\vect{x}}$, showing how well an approximate solution $\hat{\vect{x}}$ satisfies $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$. See @sec-linear-systems and @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Resonance
: The large response of a structure pushed at, or near, one of its natural frequencies. See @sec-vibrations.

Right singular vectors
: The columns $\vect{v}_i$ of $\M{V}$ in the SVD $\M{A} = \M{U}\M{\Sigma}\M{V}\T$: perpendicular input directions that $\M{A}$ sends to perpendicular output directions. See @sec-svd-pca.

Right-hand rule
: The convention that fixes which way a rotation in three dimensions is positive: point your right thumb along the axis, and your fingers curl in the positive direction. See @sec-transformations-3d.

Rigid-body mode
: A mode with natural frequency zero, in which a structure moves without stretching any spring. See @sec-vibrations.

Roller
: A truss support that can only push perpendicular to the surface it rolls on, so it provides one unknown reaction component. Compare **pin**. See @sec-trusses.

Rotation
: The transformation that turns the plane by an angle $\theta$ about the origin, with matrix $\mat{\cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta}$ for an anticlockwise turn. See @sec-transformations.

Row echelon form
: A matrix in which each row's first non-zero entry is to the right of the one above, so that all entries below the pivots are zero. See @sec-gaussian-elimination and @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Row operation
: Adding a multiple of one row to another, swapping two rows, or multiplying a row by a non-zero number. See @sec-determinants and @sec-gaussian-elimination.

Row space
: The span of the rows of a matrix. Its dimension is the rank. See @sec-fundamental-subspaces.

Row vector
: A matrix with one row. See @sec-matrices.

Row-times-column rule
: The rule for matrix multiplication: entry $(i, j)$ of $\M{A}\M{B}$ is row $i$ of $\M{A}$ dotted with column $j$ of $\M{B}$. See @sec-multiplication.

## S {#glossary-s .unnumbered}

Saddle point
: (1) A stationary point where the Hessian has both positive and negative eigenvalues, so it is a minimum in some directions and a maximum in others. See @sec-matrix-calculus. (2) An equilibrium of $\dot{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\vect{x}$ whose eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, which is unstable. See @sec-linear-odes.

Scalar
: A single number, as opposed to a vector or matrix. Multiplying by a scalar scales every entry. See @sec-arithmetic.

Scalar multiplication
: Multiplying every entry of a vector or matrix by the same number. See @sec-arithmetic.

Schrödinger equation
: The linear system $i\hbar\,\dot{\vect{\psi}} = \M{H}\vect{\psi}$ that describes how a quantum state changes in time. See @sec-physics.

Scores
: The coordinates of each item along the principal components, $\M{X}\vect{v}_i$. See @sec-svd-pca.

Scree plot
: A plot of the variance explained by each principal component against its number, used to choose how many components to keep. See @sec-data-science.

Second-order accurate
: Describes an approximation whose error is proportional to $h^2$, so that halving the grid spacing $h$ divides the error by 4. See @sec-finite-differences.

Sector
: One of the industries into which an input–output model divides an economy. See @sec-input-output.

Self-stress
: A set of member forces in a truss that balance each other with no load at all: a non-zero vector in the null space of the equilibrium matrix. See @sec-trusses.

Sensitivity
: In a population model, the rate of change of the growth rate $\lambda$ with one entry of the matrix, $\partial\lambda/\partial a_{ij}$. See **elasticity** and @sec-population-models.

Shear
: A transformation that slides lines parallel to an axis by amounts proportional to their distance from it, such as $\mat{1 & k \\ 0 & 1}$. See @sec-transformations.

Shear stress
: An off-diagonal entry of a stress matrix, which slides one side of a surface past the other. Compare **normal stress**. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Shift
: Replacing $\M{A}$ by $\M{A} - \mu\M{I}$, which subtracts $\mu$ from every eigenvalue, so that iterative eigenvalue methods find a chosen eigenvalue or converge faster. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Shifted inverse iteration
: Inverse iteration with $\M{A} - \mu\M{I}$, which finds the eigenvalue of $\M{A}$ closest to $\mu$, and its eigenvector. See @sec-eigenvalue-algorithms.

Similar matrices
: Matrices related by $\M{B} = \M{P}^{-1}\M{A}\M{P}$: the same transformation described in different bases. See @sec-basis-change.

Singular matrix
: A square matrix with determinant zero. It has no inverse, and $\M{A}\vect{x} = \vect{b}$ has either no solution or infinitely many. See @sec-determinants.

Singular value decomposition
: The factorisation $\M{A} = \M{U}\M{\Sigma}\M{V}\T$ of any matrix, with $\M{U}$ and $\M{V}$ orthogonal and the **singular values** $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge 0$ on the diagonal of $\M{\Sigma}$: rotate, stretch, rotate. See @sec-svd-pca.

Singular values
: The numbers $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge 0$ down the diagonal of $\M{\Sigma}$ in the SVD: the square roots of the eigenvalues of $\M{A}\T\M{A}$. They measure how much $\M{A}$ stretches in each direction. See @sec-svd-pca.

Singularity
: A position of a robot arm where its Jacobian is singular, so that the hand can't move in some direction at all. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

Skew-symmetric matrix
: A square matrix with $\M{A}\T = -\M{A}$. In three dimensions it represents a cross product with a fixed vector, such as an angular velocity. See @sec-physics.

Span
: The set of all linear combinations of some vectors. See @sec-span-independence.

Sparse matrix
: A matrix with so many zero entries that it pays to store and use only the non-zeros. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Spectral partitioning
: Splitting a network into two groups by the signs of the entries of its Fiedler vector. See @sec-networks.

Spectral radius
: The largest absolute value of the eigenvalues of a matrix, written $\rho(\M{T})$. An iteration with iteration matrix $\M{T}$ converges if and only if $\rho(\M{T}) < 1$. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Spectral theorem
: Every real symmetric matrix can be written $\M{Q}\M{\Lambda}\M{Q}\T$, with real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Spiral
: An equilibrium of $\dot{\vect{x}} = \M{A}\vect{x}$ with complex eigenvalues, around which solutions spiral: inwards (stable) if the real parts are negative, outwards if they are positive. See @sec-linear-odes.

Square matrix
: A matrix with as many rows as columns. See @sec-matrices.

Stable age distribution
: The proportions in each age class or stage that a population settles into: the eigenvector of the dominant eigenvalue of its projection matrix. See @sec-population-models.

Standard basis
: The columns $\ue{1}, \dots, \ue{n}$ of the identity matrix; in $\R^2$ and $\R^3$ these are $\ui$, $\uj$ and $\uk$. See @sec-basis-change.

Standard error
: A measure of the uncertainty in a fitted regression coefficient, proportional to the square root of the corresponding diagonal entry of $(\M{X}\T\M{X})^{-1}$. See @sec-data-science.

Statically determinate
: Describes a structure whose member forces are fixed by equilibrium alone: its equilibrium matrix is square and invertible. If there are more unknowns than equations it is **statically indeterminate**. See @sec-trusses.

Statically indeterminate
: Describes a structure that can carry every load, but in infinitely many ways, so that equilibrium alone doesn't fix the member forces. See **statically determinate** and @sec-trusses.

Stationary point
: A point where the gradient of a function is zero: a minimum, a maximum or a saddle point. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Steady state
: A vector left unchanged by a process $\vect{x}_{k+1} = \M{M}\vect{x}_k$: an eigenvector with eigenvalue 1. See @sec-diagonalisation and @sec-markov-pagerank.

Step size
: The distance $\alpha$ moved at each step of gradient descent, in the direction of steepest descent; also called the **learning rate**. See @sec-matrix-calculus.

Stiffness matrix
: The symmetric matrix $\M{K} = \M{B}\T\M{D}\M{B}$ relating joint displacements to applied loads, $\M{K}\vect{u} = \vect{p}$. See @sec-trusses.

Stress matrix
: The symmetric matrix that describes the forces between neighbouring pieces at a point inside a loaded material; also called the stress tensor. See @sec-symmetric-matrices.

Stretch
: The transformation $\mat{a & 0 \\ 0 & b}$, which stretches by a factor $a$ parallel to the $x$-axis and $b$ parallel to the $y$-axis. See @sec-transformations.

Stretch factor
: The number $\lambda$ by which a transformation multiplies every point of an invariant line: an eigenvalue. See @sec-invariant-lines.

Subspace
: A set of vectors that contains $\zerovec$ and is closed under adding and scaling, such as a line or plane through the origin. See @sec-span-independence.

Successive over-relaxation
: SOR: Gauss–Seidel with each update stretched by a factor $\omega$ between 0 and 2, usually above 1, to speed convergence. See @sec-iterative-methods.

Survival rate
: In a population model, the fraction of one age class that survives to join the next a step later. See @sec-population-models.

Symmetric matrix
: A square matrix equal to its transpose, so that $a_{ij} = a_{ji}$. See @sec-matrices.

## T {#glossary-t .unnumbered}

Technical coefficients matrix
: In an input–output model, the matrix $\M{A}$ whose entry $a_{ij}$ is the value of industry $i$'s product used to make £1 of industry $j$'s product. See @sec-input-output.

Tension
: The state of a truss member that is being pulled along its length. Compare **compression**. See @sec-trusses.

Thomas algorithm
: Gaussian elimination specialised to tridiagonal matrices, needing about $8n$ operations. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Tip to tail
: Adding vectors geometrically by placing the tail of the second at the tip of the first. See @sec-arithmetic.

Trace
: The sum of the diagonal entries of a square matrix, equal to the sum of its eigenvalues. See @sec-eigenvalues.

Transient state
: A state of a Markov chain that the chain eventually leaves for good. Compare **absorbing state**. See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Transition matrix
: The matrix of probabilities $m_{ij}$ of moving from state $j$ to state $i$ in one step of a Markov chain; its columns add to 1 (it is **column-stochastic**). See @sec-markov-pagerank.

Translation
: Sliding everything by a fixed vector. It isn't linear, because it moves the origin, but homogeneous coordinates turn it into a matrix multiplication. See @sec-transformations and @sec-graphics-robotics.

Transpose
: The matrix $\M{A}\T$ whose rows are the columns of $\M{A}$. See @sec-matrices.

Triangular matrix
: A square matrix that is zero below the main diagonal (upper triangular) or above it (lower triangular). See @sec-determinants.

Tridiagonal matrix
: A matrix whose only non-zero entries are on the main diagonal and the diagonals just above and below it. See @sec-cost-sparse.

Trivial solution
: The solution $\vect{x} = \zerovec$ that every homogeneous system has. See @sec-linear-systems.

Truss
: A structure of straight members joined at their ends to form triangles, as in many bridges, roofs, cranes and pylons. See @sec-trusses.

Tuned mass damper
: A large mass attached to a structure by a spring tuned to a troublesome natural frequency, which absorbs the vibration. See @sec-vibrations.

## U {#glossary-u .unnumbered}

Underdetermined system
: A system with fewer equations than unknowns. It usually has infinitely many solutions, but can have none. Compare **overdetermined system**. See @sec-gauss-jordan-rank.

Unstable method
: A method that introduces more error than the conditioning of the problem makes unavoidable. Compare **backward stable**. See @sec-floating-point-conditioning.

Upper triangular matrix
: See **triangular matrix**.

## V {#glossary-v .unnumbered}

Value added
: The part of each £1 of a sector's output that is not spent on inputs from other sectors, and so pays for wages, profits and imports. See @sec-input-output.

View matrix
: The $4 \times 4$ matrix that moves a 3D scene so that the camera sits at the origin, looking along the negative $z$ axis. See @sec-graphics-robotics.

## W {#glossary-w .unnumbered}

Walk
: A sequence of edges in a network, each starting where the last one ended. Entry $(i, j)$ of $\M{A}^k$ counts the walks of length $k$ from one node to the other. See @sec-networks.

## Z {#glossary-z .unnumbered}

Zero matrix
: The matrix whose entries are all zero, written $\M{0}$. See @sec-arithmetic.
